youtube.baslik: Electrocochleography (ECochG) and the SP/AP Ratio | Lesson 199 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
What is electrocochleography, and how is the SP/AP ratio calculated? In this lesson we cover the cochlear microphonic, summating potential and action potential, transtympanic and extratympanic electrodes, and the diagnostic value of an increased SP/AP ratio in endolymphatic hydrops.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Hall, New Handbook of Auditory Evoked Responses; Katz, Handbook of Clinical Audiology; Lopez-Escamez et al., Diagnostic criteria for Meniere's disease, Journal of Vestibular Research (2015); Ayub et al., A systematic review and meta-analysis of extratympanic electrocochleography in Ménière's disease diagnosis, International Journal of Audiology (2019).

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.alt: The electrophysiological recording closest to the cochlea
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.

cumleler.yazi: In this lesson we will learn about electrocochleography, or ECochG, and the three components seen in this recording.
cumleler.ses: In this lesson we will learn about electrocochleography, or E cock G, and the three components seen in this recording.

cumleler: We will cover electrode types, how the summating to action potential ratio is calculated, and its link to endolymphatic hydrops.
Electrocochleography records the electrical potentials that sound produces in the cochlea and the first part of the auditory nerve.

cumleler.yazi: These responses appear within the first few milliseconds after the stimulus, so ECochG belongs to the early responses.
cumleler.ses: These responses appear within the first few milliseconds after the stimulus, so E cock G belongs to the early responses.

cumleler: The first two components come from the hair cells; they are the cochlear microphonic and the summating potential.
Outer hair cells contribute most to the cochlear microphonic; inner and outer hair cells together contribute to the summating potential.
The third component is the action potential, produced by the synchronous firing of auditory nerve fibers.
The closer the electrode is to the cochlea, the larger and clearer these small responses are recorded.

cumleler.yazi: So ECochG can be thought of as the electrophysiological recording taken from the point closest to the cochlea.
cumleler.ses: So E cock G can be thought of as the electrophysiological recording taken from the point closest to the cochlea.

ogeler.metin: Follows the stimulus; flips with polarity.
A direct current shift of baseline.
The nerve response; ABR wave I.

cumleler.yazi: The cochlear microphonic, or CM, is an alternating current response that closely follows the waveform of the stimulus.
cumleler.ses: The cochlear microphonic, or C M, is an alternating current response that closely follows the waveform of the stimulus.

cumleler.yazi: When the stimulus polarity changes, the CM flips too, so it cancels out when the two polarities are averaged.
cumleler.ses: When the stimulus polarity changes, the C M flips too, so it cancels out when the two polarities are averaged.

cumleler.yazi: The summating potential, or SP, is a direct current like component that shifts the baseline in one direction while the stimulus lasts.
cumleler.ses: The summating potential, or S P, is a direct current like component that shifts the baseline in one direction while the stimulus lasts.

cumleler.yazi: The SP does not change direction with polarity, so it remains in the recording with alternating polarity.
cumleler.ses: The S P does not change direction with polarity, so it remains in the recording with alternating polarity.

cumleler.yazi: The action potential, or AP, is the compound response of the auditory nerve, and its first negative peak is called N1.
cumleler.ses: The action potential, or A P, is the compound response of the auditory nerve, and its first negative peak is called N one.

cumleler.yazi: The AP is the same response as wave I of the auditory brainstem response, or ABR; its latency is about one and a half milliseconds.
cumleler.ses: The A P is the same response as wave one of the auditory brainstem response, or ABR; its latency is about one and a half milliseconds.

cumleler.yazi: This schematic drawing shows an example ECochG recording obtained with an alternating polarity click.
cumleler.ses: This schematic drawing shows an example E cock G recording obtained with an alternating polarity click.

cumleler: Measurement starts by setting the baseline of the recording.

cumleler.yazi: Just before the AP, a small shoulder departs from the baseline; this is the SP.
cumleler.ses: Just before the A P, a small shoulder departs from the baseline; this is the S P.

cumleler.yazi: Then comes a sharp, large peak; this is the N1 peak of the AP.
cumleler.ses: Then comes a sharp, large peak; this is the N one peak of the A P.

cumleler: Depending on the recording system, these peaks may be plotted up or down; what matters is using the same measurement rule.

cumleler.yazi: The SP and AP amplitudes are measured from the baseline to the relevant point.
cumleler.ses: The S P and A P amplitudes are measured from the baseline to the relevant point.

cumleler.yazi: The SP amplitude is divided by the AP amplitude; the result is called the SP/AP ratio.
cumleler.ses: The S P amplitude is divided by the A P amplitude; the result is called the S P to A P ratio.

cumleler.yazi: In ECochG, the location of the active electrode is the most important factor in the size and quality of the recording.
cumleler.ses: In E cock G, the location of the active electrode is the most important factor in the size and quality of the recording.

cumleler: In the transtympanic method, a fine needle electrode is passed through the eardrum and placed on the promontory.
The promontory is the bulge formed by the basal turn of the cochlea on the medial wall of the middle ear.
This is done by a physician under local anesthesia; the largest and clearest responses are obtained with this method.
In the tympanic method, a soft-tipped electrode is made to touch the surface of the eardrum; the eardrum is not pierced.
In the extratympanic method, the electrode sits in the ear canal; foam-tipped electrodes called tiptrodes are a common example.
The farther the electrode is from the cochlea, the smaller the response and the more averaging is needed.
The reference electrode is usually on the opposite ear or mastoid, and the ground electrode on the forehead.

ogeler.metin: Largest response; invasive, done by a physician.
Comfortable; small response, sensitive to noise.

cumleler: Transtympanic recording gives the largest response, but it is invasive and not offered in every center.
Tympanic recording gives a larger response than extratympanic recording without being invasive, but eardrum contact can be uncomfortable.
Extratympanic recording is the most comfortable method, but the responses are small and the recording is more sensitive to noise.
Whichever method is chosen, normal values are specific to that method and that laboratory.
So a ratio obtained in one center is not compared with the cutoff values of another method.

cumleler.yazi: ECochG usually uses a high-level click or tone burst, at about ninety decibels.
cumleler.ses: E cock G usually uses a high-level click or tone burst, at about ninety decibels.

cumleler.yazi: Alternating polarity is preferred for measuring the SP and AP, so the CM and stimulus artifact cancel out in the average.
cumleler.ses: Alternating polarity is preferred for measuring the S P and A P, so the C M and stimulus artifact cancel out in the average.

cumleler.yazi: If the CM is to be studied, rarefaction and condensation polarities are recorded separately and the two recordings are compared.
cumleler.ses: If the C M is to be studied, rarefaction and condensation polarities are recorded separately and the two recordings are compared.

cumleler.yazi: Because the SP is a slow, direct current like potential, the high-pass filter is set very low.
cumleler.ses: Because the S P is a slow, direct current like potential, the high-pass filter is set very low.

cumleler.yazi: The SP can be seen more clearly with a tone burst, so some centers also record with a tone burst.
cumleler.ses: The S P can be seen more clearly with a tone burst, so some centers also record with a tone burst.

cumleler: The time window is short, and each recording is obtained at least twice to confirm repeatability.

cumleler.yazi: The best-known use of ECochG is to look for endolymphatic hydrops, that is, excess fluid in the scala media.
cumleler.ses: The best-known use of E cock G is to look for endolymphatic hydrops, that is, excess fluid in the scala media.

cumleler: The gray dashed line shows an example normal recording, and the blue line an example recording from an ear with hydrops.
In hydrops, the extra endolymph pushes the basilar membrane in one direction and disturbs the symmetry of its motion.

cumleler.yazi: As a result, the direct current response of the hair cells, the SP, grows, while the AP does not grow to the same degree.
cumleler.ses: As a result, the direct current response of the hair cells, the S P, grows, while the A P does not grow to the same degree.

cumleler.yazi: So the SP/AP ratio rises, and the shoulder before the AP becomes clearly wider in the recording.
cumleler.ses: So the S P to A P ratio rises, and the shoulder before the A P becomes clearly wider in the recording.

cumleler.yazi: With extratympanic and tympanic recording, an SP larger than about half the AP is considered increased in most laboratories.
cumleler.ses: With extratympanic and tympanic recording, an S P larger than about half the A P is considered increased in most laboratories.

cumleler: With transtympanic recording the cutoff may be lower; the exact value is always set by the laboratory's own norms.

cumleler.yazi: Now let us interpret an ECochG result obtained with extratympanic recording, using purely example values.
cumleler.ses: Now let us interpret an E cock G result obtained with extratympanic recording, using purely example values.

cumleler.yazi: In the right ear the SP is zero point three and the AP is one microvolt; the ratio is zero point three zero.
cumleler.ses: In the right ear the S P is zero point three and the A P is one microvolt; the ratio is zero point three zero.

cumleler.yazi: In the left ear the SP is zero point six and the AP is again one microvolt; the ratio is zero point six zero.
cumleler.ses: In the left ear the S P is zero point six and the A P is again one microvolt; the ratio is zero point six zero.

cumleler: In this example, let the laboratory's upper limit of normal be zero point five zero.
In that case the ratio in the left ear is considered increased, and the finding may be consistent with endolymphatic hydrops.
This result alone does not make a diagnosis; it is passed to the physician together with the history, serial audiograms and other tests.
The report gives the values for both ears, the electrode used and the laboratory cutoff together.

maddeler.metin: A normal ratio _does not exclude_ it

yan.metin: A normal ratio *does not exclude* hydrops

cumleler.yazi: An increased SP/AP ratio, together with a fitting history and audiogram, supports the suspicion of endolymphatic hydrops.
cumleler.ses: An increased S P to A P ratio, together with a fitting history and audiogram, supports the suspicion of endolymphatic hydrops.

cumleler: But a normal ratio does not exclude hydrops; many people with Meniere's disease have a normal ratio.
A meta-analysis of studies using extratympanic recording found a sensitivity of about fifty percent.
The same analysis reported a higher specificity, of about eighty four percent.
Some studies report higher sensitivity with transtympanic recording and tone burst stimuli; results vary between centers.
Findings may also vary with the stage of the disease and how close the recording is to an attack.

cumleler.yazi: As we saw in the lesson on Meniere's disease, diagnosis rests on clinical criteria; ECochG is a supporting test.
cumleler.ses: As we saw in the lesson on Meniere's disease, diagnosis rests on clinical criteria; E cock G is a supporting test.

cumleler.yazi: Besides the amplitude ratio, some centers also use the ratio of the areas under the SP and AP curves.
cumleler.ses: Besides the amplitude ratio, some centers also use the ratio of the areas under the S P and A P curves.

ogeler.metin: Raised ratio in superior canal dehiscence.
Ear canal electrode in unclear ABR.
Monitoring in ear and brainstem surgery.

cumleler.yazi: An increased SP/AP ratio has also been reported in third window disorders such as superior canal dehiscence.
cumleler.ses: An increased S P to A P ratio has also been reported in third window disorders such as superior canal dehiscence.

cumleler.yazi: In auditory neuropathy, ECochG may show a large cochlear microphonic with an abnormal or absent AP.
cumleler.ses: In auditory neuropathy, E cock G may show a large cochlear microphonic with an abnormal or absent A P.

cumleler: This finding suggests that the hair cells work but neural synchrony is disrupted.

cumleler.yazi: If wave I is unclear on the ABR, an ear canal electrode enlarges wave I and helps measure the interpeak latencies.
cumleler.ses: If wave one is unclear on the ABR, an ear canal electrode enlarges wave one and helps measure the interpeak latencies.

cumleler: It is also used to monitor hearing during ear and brainstem surgery; we will cover this in a later lesson.
Otoscopy comes before recording; wax or discharge in the ear canal affects both electrode contact and patient safety.
The electrode is placed according to the chosen method, and the patient is asked whether they are comfortable.
Electrode impedance is checked; high or unbalanced impedance leads to a noisy recording.
The recording is taken at a high level and repeated at least once under the same conditions.

cumleler.yazi: The baseline, SP and AP points are marked, the amplitudes are measured, and the ratio is calculated.
cumleler.ses: The baseline, S P and A P points are marked, the amplitudes are measured, and the ratio is calculated.

cumleler: The report must state the electrode method, stimulus, level, polarity and the laboratory's normal limit.

sahneler.metin: Decide where to measure the baseline before you record; if the SP and AP are not measured by the same rule, the ratio will mislead.

cumleler.yazi: A tip from the field: the SP/AP ratio is very sensitive to where the baseline is placed.
cumleler.ses: A tip from the field: the S P to A P ratio is very sensitive to where the baseline is placed.

cumleler.yazi: Mark the baseline and the SP point by the same rule in every recording; a small shift can change the ratio markedly.
cumleler.ses: Mark the baseline and the S P point by the same rule in every recording; a small shift can change the ratio markedly.

cumleler.yazi: Overlay the repeated recordings; a shoulder that does not appear in the same place in both should not be read as an SP.
cumleler.ses: Overlay the repeated recordings; a shoulder that does not appear in the same place in both should not be read as an S P.

cumleler: In doubtful results, repeating the recording with a different stimulus, such as a tone burst, strengthens the interpretation.

maddeler.metin: A normal ratio _does not exclude_ hydrops

cumleler.yazi: ECochG records the cochlear microphonic, summating potential and action potential; the AP is the same response as ABR wave I.
cumleler.ses: E cock G records the cochlear microphonic, summating potential and action potential; the A P is the same response as ABR wave one.

cumleler: There are transtympanic, tympanic and extratympanic electrodes; the closer the electrode to the cochlea, the larger the response.

cumleler.yazi: In endolymphatic hydrops the SP grows, and the SP/AP ratio rises.
cumleler.ses: In endolymphatic hydrops the S P grows, and the S P to A P ratio rises.

cumleler: The ratio has moderate sensitivity; a normal result does not exclude hydrops, and diagnosis rests on clinical criteria.

sahneler.soru: What is expected on ECochG in hydrops?
sahneler.aciklama: In hydrops the _SP grows_, and the SP/AP ratio rises.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: in endolymphatic hydrops, which finding is expected on the ECochG recording?
cumleler.ses: Test yourself: in endolymphatic hydrops, which finding is expected on the E cock G recording?

cumleler.yazi: The correct answer is A: a raised SP/AP ratio.
cumleler.ses: The correct answer is A: a raised S P to A P ratio.

cumleler.yazi: Extra endolymph disturbs the symmetric motion of the basilar membrane, and the summating potential grows; the AP does not grow as much.
cumleler.ses: Extra endolymph disturbs the symmetric motion of the basilar membrane, and the summating potential grows; the A P does not grow as much.
